text.p: British supermarket chain Asda Plc said on Tuesday it would defend a writ from food and drink giant Grand Metropolitan Plc "vigourously and robustly," saying there was "no case to answer."

GrandMet served a writ on Asda on Friday alleging that four of the supermarkets own brands -- Daniel Boone's, Deep South, ASDA Peach Schnapps and Windward -- could be mistaken for GrandMet's branded equivalent. "We invite everyone to put ASDA brands to the test. We're confident that they will agree these are "taste-alike' and not "look-alike' products," said Justin King, ASDA Brand director in a statement.

"Not only do ASDA brand spirits look dissimilar to Grand Metropolitan's, there is another important difference for shoppers and it's one they can pocket -- our Daniel Boone bourbon, for example, is 12.23 pounds ($20.22) compared to 16.73 pounds for Jack Daniels," said King.
Since the launch of ASDA brand spirits in October, the supermarket's overall sales of spirits have increased while sales of branded equivalents have remained constant, he added.

"Clearly until now people have been priced out of the spirits market by the "Brand Tax,' said King. ASDA calculates that its Deep South is 4.04 pounds cheaper than the same-sized bottle of GrandMet's Southern Comfort at 14.73 pounds.

ASDA is out to break the resale price maintenance on over- the-counter medicines. Britain's retail price maintenance is currently under review by competition watchdog the Office of Fair Trading. ($1=.6047 Pound)
